Rashi on Shabbat 124b:11:1.hebrew: לצוק לתוכה מקפה - עבה, דומיא דעיסה מעורבת במים:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:11:1.english: To pour mikpeh into it - [It is] thick, similar to dough mixed with water.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:13:1.english: Since they were prepared via their original [vessels] - When the day became sanctified [at the onset of Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:14:1.hebrew: מסיקין בכלים - ביו"ט, שהרי ראוין לטלטל, ויטלטל ויתנם לתוך האור:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:14:1.english: One may kindle [a fire] with vessels - On a Festival, since they are fit to be moved, and one may move [them] and place them into the fire.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:14:2.english: And one may not kindle with shards of vessels - For they are muktzeh [set aside] and are not fit for handling.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:15:1.english: They are ordinary wood - For they have been [designated] for kindling since yesterday.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:15:2.hebrew: וקתני אין מסיקין - ולא אמרינן מוכנין היו אגב אביהן, אלא אמרינן נולד נינהו ואסירי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:15:2.english: And it teaches: One may not kindle - And we do not say they were prepared [beforehand] by virtue of their parent [vessel]; rather, we say they are nolad [newly created] and are prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:16:1.hebrew: מר סבר מוכן הוא - כיון דראוי לשום מלאכה. ומר סבר נולד הוה, דמאתמול לאו להאי מלאכה הוה קאי, הלכך, מעין מלאכתו בעינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:16:1.english: This Sage holds it was prepared - since it is fit for some function. And this Sage holds it is nolad [newly emerged], because yesterday it was not designated for this function; therefore, we require [a function] similar to its [original] function.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:1.hebrew: הא רבי יהודה - מסיקין בכלים ואין מסיקין בשברי כלים, דאית ליה מוקצה ונולד. כלים לאו מוקצה נינהו, שברים נולד נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Yehuda - [This refers to the baraita stating that] one may kindle [a fire] with vessels, but one may not kindle with broken vessels, for he holds [the prohibitions of] muktzeh [set-aside] and nolad [newly-arisen]. Vessels are not muktzeh; broken [vessels] are nolad.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:2.english: And this [one] - [the baraita] that teaches that one may kindle with both of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:3.english: Rabbi Shimon - For he does not hold [the prohibition of] muktzeh and he does not hold [the prohibition of] nolad.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:4.english: And this - [refers to the baraita] in which it was taught: even with [whole] vessels one may not kindle.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:5.hebrew: רבי נחמיה היא - דאמר אין כלי ניטל אלא לצורך תשמישו המיוחד לו, והאי לאו מיוחד הוא לו, דלאו להסקה קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:18:5.english: It is [according to] Rabbi Nehemiah - Who says a vessel may only be handled for the sake of its designated use, and this [kindling] is not designated for it, since it is not meant for kindling.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:19:1.hebrew: דאייתור - שהשלים בניינו וניתותר, ומהשתא לא קיימי לבנין אלא לישב עליהם, ותורת כלי עליהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:19:1.english: That were left over - [Meaning] that he completed his building and [they] were left over, and from now on they are not designated for building, rather to sit on them, and the status of a vessel applies to them.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:19:2.hebrew: שרגינהו - אי סדרן זו על זו, ודאי אקצינהו לצורך בנין אחר:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:19:2.english: [If] he stacked them - If he arranged them one on top of another, he certainly set them aside for the need of another building.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:1:1.hebrew: אין מוציאין - הוצאה שלא לצורך, דלא אישתרי לכתחילה ביו"ט טפי מבשבת אלא אוכל נפש. והך דמשילין — ב"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:1:1.english: One may not carry out - [This refers to] carrying out that is not for [food] need, for initially [carrying] was not permitted on a Festival more than on Shabbat except for food [preparation]. And this [mishna] of lowering [produce] is [in accordance with] Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:1.hebrew: בחצר - דשכיחי בה כלים שהחרס הזה ראוי להם לכיסוי, ותורת כלי עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:1.english: In the courtyard - For vessels are common there for which this shard is fit as a cover, and [thus] it has the status of a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:2.hebrew: אבל לא בכרמלית - אפי' בתוך ד' אמות, דלא שכיחי ביה מאני ולא חזי לכסויי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:2.english: But not in a karmelit - Even within four cubits, because vessels are not common there and it is not fit for covering.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:3.hebrew: אפילו בכרמלית - הואיל ולאו רה"ר הוא, שכיחי דאזלי ויתבי התם, וחזי לכסות בו רוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:3.english: Even in a karmelit - Since it is not a public domain, it is common that [people] go and sit there, and [the shard] is fit to cover spittle with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:4.hebrew: ורבא אמר אף ברה"ר - כיון דבחצר כלי הוא, בעלמא נמי לא פקע שם כלי מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:20:4.english: And Rava said: Even in the public domain - Since in a courtyard it is [considered] a vessel, elsewhere as well the status of a vessel does not depart from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:1.english: In ritka - The name of a public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:2.english: His shoes became dirty with clay - His shoe became dirty with clay.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:4.hebrew: אמר רבא לא מסתייה דלא גמירי - מה אסור, מה מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:4.english: Rava said: Is it not enough that they have not learned - what is forbidden [and] what is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:5.english: Rather, they also teach - They teach the error that is in their hands to others.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:6.hebrew: לדידי - לקינוח, ואע"ג דלא שכיח, הרי שם כלי עליו בחצר:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:21:6.english: To me - For wiping, and even though it is not common, behold, it has the status of a vessel in a courtyard.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:2.english: A seal - [a seal] of a jug, where the jug was crushed.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:4.english: And its shards - [those] of a jug may be moved on Shabbat, since they are fit for covering a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:5.hebrew: לא יספות - יתקן להתיר בליטותיו ועוקציו בשבת, דעביד כלי והוי מכה בפטיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:5.english: One may not break - [He may not] fashion [it] to remove its protrusions and sharp points on Shabbat, for he is making a utensil, and it is [considered] striking with a hammer.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:6.hebrew: ואם זרק - מגופה זו לאשפה, בטלה מתורת כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:22:6.english: And if one threw - this [clay] seal into the garbage, it is nullified from the status of a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:23:1.hebrew: זרקיה לגלימיה - בשבת לאשפה, ה"נ דאסור לטלטולי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:23:1.english: [If] he threw his cloak - on Shabbat onto a garbage heap, [is it] also so that it is prohibited to move it?

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:2:1.hebrew: טלטול מי שמעת להו - דמשוי יו"ט לשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:2:1.english: Did you hear them [prohibit] moving [an object] - That they equate Yom Tov to Shabbat?

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:2:2.hebrew: טלטול לאו לצורך הוצאה - בתמיה. הלכך, אי מזלזלת בטלטול, מזלזלת בהוצאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:2:2.english: Moving [is] not for the purpose of carrying out - [This is said] as a rhetorical question. Therefore, if you treat moving lightly, you will treat carrying out lightly.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:3:1.english: In accordance with this [statement] of Rava - Who said [that moving an object for] the need of its place is like [moving it for] the need of [the object] itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:3:2.english: A hoe [mar] - [In Old French,] fossoir [a hoe/mattock].

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:3:3.hebrew: שלא יגנב - דומיא דמחמה לצל, ואסור בדבר שמלאכתו לאיסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:3:3.english: So that it will not be stolen - [This is] similar to [moving an object] from the sun to the shade, and it is prohibited in the case of an object whose [primary] use is for a prohibited [labor].

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:4:2.hebrew: לאו למימרא כו' - למה לי לפרושי בהדיא דליתיב עלה? לאו משום למימרא דהאי דשרי לטלטולי, משום דצורך גופו הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:4:2.english: Is that not to say, etc. - Why did he need to specify explicitly "that he may sit on it"? [Is it] not in order to say that [the reason] it is permitted to move [it] is because it is for the purpose of [using] the object itself?

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:5:1.hebrew: שקילו שותא מקמיה כהנא - דניתוב על מקומה קאמר, וצורך מקומה הוא דהוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:5:1.english: Remove the net from before Kahana - He is saying [this] so that he may sit in its place, and it was [a case of] needing its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:5:2.hebrew: מחמה לצל הוה - במקום הרע לה היתה, ואי לאו דפריש בהדיא "ליתיב עלה", מאן דחזי סבר דמחמה לצל שרי. ולמקומה לא היה צריך, דלימא שישב במקומה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:5:2.english: It was from the sun to the shade - [The net] was in a place that was harmful to it, and had [Rav] not explicitly stated, "Let him sit on it," anyone who saw [it being moved] would think that [moving a vessel] from the sun to the shade is permitted. And there was no need for its place, that he should say that he should sit in its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:1.english: Cushions [bei sadyota] - Pillows of felt, which they call feltre [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:2.english: In the sun - In the sun.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:3.hebrew: אמר ליה שרי - רבא לטעמיה, דאמר דבר שמלאכתו להיתר אף מחמה לצל מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:3.english: He said to him: It is permitted - Rava [follows] his own reasoning, for he says [that] an item whose [primary] use is for a permitted [purpose] is permitted [to be moved] even from the sun to the shade.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:4.english: I have others - I do not need it itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:5.hebrew: דכרבה סבירא לך - דאמר מחמה לצל אסור. והלכה כרבא, דאמר: דבר שמלאכתו להיתר שרי לגמרי, ודבר שמלאכתו לאיסור — לצורך גופו ומקומו מותר, מחמה לצל ושלא יגנב אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:6:5.english: That you hold in accordance with Rabbah - Who says [that moving an object whose primary use is permitted] from the sun to the shade is prohibited. And the halakhah follows Rava, who says: An object whose primary use is permitted is completely permitted [to be moved], while an object whose primary use is prohibited — for its own use or its place it is permitted, [but] from the sun to the shade or so that it not be stolen is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:7:1.english: Brooms - [In Old French,] escobe [a broom], with which one sweeps the table.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:7:2.hebrew: של מילתא - בגדים לכבד שולחן, שמלאכתו להיתר:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:7:2.english: Of fine wool - Garments [used] to sweep a table, whose work is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:7:3.hebrew: של תמרה - כעין שלנו, לכבד את הבית, דאסור משום אשווי גומות, דמודה רבי שמעון בפסיק רישיה ולא ימות:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:7:3.english: Of date-palm [fronds] - Like ours, for sweeping the house, which is prohibited on account of leveling holes [in the ground], for Rabbi Shimon concedes [that it is prohibited] in [a case of] pesik reishei velo yamut [an inevitable consequence].

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:8:1.english: For the purpose of [the object] itself - For a permitted task.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:8:2.hebrew: אלא מחמה לצל, בהא לימא רבי אלעזר אף של תמרה - דבר שמלאכתו לאיסור, ליכא מאן דשרי מחמה לצל:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:8:2.english: Rather, from the sun to the shade; in this [case], would Rabbi Elazar say even [a broom] of date-palm [fronds]? - [As for] an object whose [primary] use is for a forbidden [activity], there is no one who permits [moving it] from the sun to the shade.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:8:3.hebrew: וכן אמר רבי אלעזר - של מילתא מותר, של תמרה אסור מחמה לצל:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:8:3.english: And so too, Rabbi Elazar said - [That] of fine wool is permitted; [that] of date-palm [fronds] is prohibited [to be moved] from the sun to the shade.

Rashi on Shabbat 124b:9:1.hebrew: מעין מלאכה - שום מלאכה, ואפי' אינה מעין הראשונה:
Rashi on Shabbat 124b:9:1.english: A semblance of work - [That is,] some work, even if it is not like the original [work].

Tosafot on Shabbat 124b:18:1.hebrew: הא רבי נחמיה - דסבירא ליה דאין כלי ניטל אלא לצורך תשמישו הרגיל בחול, כדמפרש בפרק במה מדליקין (לעיל שבת דף לו.), והאי נמי אין רגיל בחול לשרוף אותו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 124b:18:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Neḥemya - For he holds that a utensil may only be moved for the purpose of its usual use on a weekday, as [the Gemara] explains in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (above, Shabbat 36a), and this [utensil] too is not usually burned on a weekday.

Tosafot on Shabbat 124b:20:1.hebrew: ורבא אמר אפילו ברה"ר - ובהני דנשברו בע"ש קאמר, דאי בנשברו בשבת, האמר בפרק נוטל (לקמן שבת דף קמב:) דרבא אית ליה מוקצה, וכל שכן נולד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 124b:20:1.english: "And Rava said: Even in the public domain" - And [he] is speaking about those [shards] that broke on the eve of Shabbat, for if [they] broke on Shabbat, surely he said in the chapter [entitled] Noteil (below, Shabbat 142b) that Rava holds of muktzeh, and all the more so nolad.
